paragraphs: In Sifrei, Balak, at the source locator פכ״ה-ג [compare Sifrei Bamidbar 131], there is an incident involving Pinchas ben Guvta d’Arich; in Jerusalem Talmud Sanhedrin 10:2, the reading is an incident involving Menachem of Gufta Aryeh.

notes.text: Hyman gives the Sifrei locator as פכ״ה-ג. Whether this identifies a biblical chapter and verse or a section requires checking. The two names and place forms differ.

The saved whole Wikisource Sifrei Bamidbar131 scalar contains Pinchas ben Guvta d’Arich in the Peor account; the saved whole Guggenheimer Sanhedrin10:2 scalar instead has Menachem of Gufta Ariach. These supply matching passages while preserving בן/איש and Aryeh/Ariach differences. The frozen פכ״ה-ג may be a Numbers25:3 locator, but that reading and any printed history are not established by the digital comparison.

The consulted scan of Hyman, volume I, printed p. 301, gives the Guvta d’Arich notice with the compact Sifrei locator פכ״ה-ג and the two forms פנחס בן גובתא דאריח and מנחם איש גופתא אריה. The directly consulted digital Sifrei Bamidbar 131 has פינחס בן גובתא דאריח in the Peor story, while the consulted Guggenheimer Yerushalmi Sanhedrin 10:2 reads מנחם איש גופתה אריח. The English retains Hyman’s compact locator and uses 131 only as a comparison; this does not establish an exact historical edition-numbering map. The earlier notes describe the state before the printed-page inspection. The different personal names, בן/איש, and place-like spellings remain distinct without an authority identity or locality identification.
